### Group Members

Xinying Zou (xz3593) · Chen Li (cl4946) · Rachel Liu (rl3721) · Fan Bu (fb2731) · Yihui Luo (yl6378)

### Motivation

NYC restaurant letter grades offer diners a quick summary of inspection outcomes, but they do not show which violations were recorded. Even restaurants with the same grade can differ in inspection scores and critical violations. We will examine how critical violations vary across NYC neighborhoods and what diners can learn by comparing restaurants within the same grade.

### Research Questions

1. How does the proportion of restaurants with at least one critical violation differ across neighborhoods and boroughs?
2. How do inspection scores and critical violations differ among restaurants with the same letter grade?
3. Which types of critical violations are most common, and do their patterns vary by location?

### Intended Final Products

We will create a project website with an interactive map of inspection outcomes and a side-by-side tool for comparing two restaurants' grades, scores, and cited violations. The website will also feature a reproducible report, supporting visualizations, and a two-minute narrated screencast.

### Anticipated Data Source

We will use the public [NYC DOHMH Restaurant Inspection Results](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/43nn-pn8j) dataset, which includes restaurant identifiers, inspection dates, grades, scores, violation descriptions, critical-violation flags, and location information.

### Planned Analyses and Visualizations

- **Data preparation and EDA:** Combine violation-level rows into inspection-level records; select each restaurant's most recent eligible graded inspection; summarize grade, score, and critical-violation distributions.
- **Geographic patterns:** Use `leaflet` to map restaurants and display neighborhood-level percentages of restaurants with critical violations, alongside restaurant counts. We will use borough-level summaries if neighborhood samples are too small.
- **Within-grade comparisons:** Use `ggplot2` or `plotly` to compare scores and critical-violation patterns among restaurants with the same grade.
- **Violation types and restaurant comparison:** Summarize common critical violations by area and allow users to compare two restaurants' inspection records side by side.

### Coding Challenges

We will avoid double-counting violations from the same inspection, distinguish restaurants using unique IDs, handle missing grades and locations, and check whether neighborhood boundaries can be matched reliably. Building a responsive interactive map and restaurant comparison tool will be an additional challenge. We will document exclusions and maintain a reproducible data-cleaning workflow.
